column2: 由 un-（反向）＋ load（装载）构成；load 一支 ← 古英语 lād（载运、路）← 原始日耳曼语 *laidō
column3: to take goods off a vehicle
column5: They unloaded the van in ten minutes.|He unloaded his worries onto a friend.
column6: taking off what was put on – 把装上去的东西再取下来
column7: 卸货：把货物从车船上搬下|卸下：把负载或负担去掉|倒出：把心里的话一并说给人听

column2: 中古英语 until，或为 unto 的北部变体；由 un-（朝、至）＋ till（到）构成，till 反倒是它的词根而非缩写
column3: up to the time that something happens
column5: Wait until the light turns green.|The shop is closed until Monday.
column6: marking where a stretch of time stops – 标出一段时间到哪儿为止
column7: 直到：一直持续到那一刻|在…之前：从反面说同一条界

column2: 由 un-（不）＋ usual（通常的）构成；usual 一支 ← 古法语 usuel ← 拉丁语 usualis ← usus（惯用）
column3: not what normally happens or is seen
column5: It is unusual for him to be late.|The coin has an unusual shape.
column6: standing outside what one is used to – 落在人所习惯的范围之外
column7: 不寻常的：与平常情况不同|罕见的：出现的次数极少

column2: 中古英语 up ← 古英语 upp ← 原始日耳曼语 *upp（上）
column3: toward or in a higher position
column5: The balloon drifted up over the roof.|Stand up when he comes in.
column6: in the direction away from the ground – 朝离开地面的那个方向
column7: 向上：动作朝高处进行|起来：由卧或坐转为立|往高处：位置移到更高的地方

column2: 中古英语 voice ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 voiz／古法语 vois ← 拉丁语 vocem（vox「声音」的宾格）；取代了古英语 stefn
column3: the sound a person makes when speaking or singing
column5: She has a low, clear voice.|Workers voiced their concerns at the meeting.
column6: the sound a person's own throat produces – 人自己喉间发出的那种声音
column7: 嗓音：某人说话唱歌的音色|说出：把想法用声音表达出来|发言权：能把意见说出来的那份资格

column2: 中古英语 voide ← 古法语 vuit／voide ← 通俗拉丁语 *vocitum ← 拉丁语 vacuus（空的）
column3: empty, or having no legal force
column5: The contract is now void.|He stared into the void beyond the cliff.
column6: having nothing in it, so it counts for nothing – 里面什么也没有，因而也不算数
column7: 空的：内里没有东西|无效的：法律上不成立，等于没有|虚空：什么都没有的那一片

column2: 借自意大利语 vulcano ← 地名 Vulcano（第勒尼安海上的火山小岛）← 拉丁语 Vulcanus（罗马火神）
column3: a mountain with an opening through which hot rock is thrown out
column5: The volcano erupted without warning.|Ash from the volcano closed the airport.
column6: a mountain with a vent that throws out molten rock – 山上有口，从里面喷出熔岩的那种山

column2: 由 volley（凌空击球）＋ ball（球）构成；1895 年创制时原名 Mintonette，1896 年因其凌空对击的打法改称 volley ball
column3: a game in which two teams hit a ball over a high net with their hands
column5: They play volleyball on the beach.|She joined the school volleyball team.
column6: a game of striking a ball over a net before it lands – 趁球未落地就把它击过网的比赛

column2: 以意大利物理学家 Alessandro Volta 之名命名；他是现代电池的发明者
column3: the unit used to measure electrical force
column5: The battery supplies twelve volts.|A shock of several thousand volts is fatal.
column6: the unit that measures how hard electricity is pushed – 计量电被推得多用力的那个单位
column7: 伏特：这个单位的全称|伏：日常与标注中的简称

column2: 由 volt ＋ -age 构成；volt 一支出自意大利物理学家 Alessandro Volta 之名
column3: the amount of electrical force in a circuit, measured in volts
column5: Check the voltage before plugging it in.|High voltage can arc across a gap.
column6: how much electrical push there is between two points – 两点之间电被推的力度有多大

column2: 中古英语 voluntarie ← 古法语 volontaire ← 拉丁语 voluntarius（出于自愿的）← voluntas（意愿）← volo（愿、要）；取代了古英语 selfwille
column3: done by choice, not because one is made to
column5: Attendance at the meeting is entirely voluntary.|She does voluntary work at the clinic.
column6: done because one chose to, with no compulsion – 出于自己选择，没人强迫
column7: 自愿的：本人愿意才做|志愿的：不取报酬、主动去做的那种

column2: 借自中古法语 voluntaire ← 拉丁语 voluntarius（自愿的）；或由英语 voluntary ＋ -eer 构成
column3: a person who offers to do something without being paid
column5: Volunteers cleared the riverbank last weekend.|He volunteered to drive them home.
column6: one who steps forward without being asked or paid – 没人叫、也不要钱就站出来的人
column7: 志愿者：主动无偿做事的那个人|自愿参加：主动报名去做这个动作

column2: 源自拉丁语 votum（誓愿、许愿）← voveō（立誓）← 原始印欧语 *h₁wegʷʰ-（许诺、立誓）；与 vow 同源
column3: a formal choice made in an election or decision
column5: Each member has one vote.|They voted to delay the decision.
column6: the single formal choice each person is allowed – 每人被允许表达的那一份正式选择
column7: 选票：投出去的那张纸或那一份|表决：以计票方式作决定|投票权：有资格投出那一份的权利

column2: 中古英语 vowel ← 古法语 vouel ← 拉丁语 vocalis（发声的）← vox（声音）；是希腊语 phoneen 的意译借词
column3: a speech sound made with the mouth open and air flowing freely
column5: English has more vowel sounds than letters.|Stress falls on the second vowel.
column6: a sound made with the breath passing out unblocked – 气流不受阻挡地出去所成的音
column7: 元音：语音学上的正式称法|母音：另一种译法，义同

column2: 中古英语 viage ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 viage／古法语 voiage ← 拉丁语 viaticum（旅费、行装）← via（路）；今拼写受现代法语 voyage 影响
column3: a long journey by sea or in space
column5: The voyage took eleven weeks.|They set out on a voyage to the Arctic.
column6: a long journey across water or space – 越过海面或太空的一趟长途
column7: 航行：船或航天器的行进|远航：路程特别长的那种航行

column2: 中古英语 vulgare ← 拉丁语 vulgaris（属于民众的）← vulgus（民众、群氓）← 原始印欧语 *welH-
column3: lacking taste or good manners
column5: He told a vulgar joke at dinner.|The decoration struck her as vulgar.
column6: coarse in a way that marks it as common – 粗到一看便知不上台面
column7: 粗俗的：言行不雅|庸俗的：趣味低下、格调不高

column2: 借自晚期拉丁语 vulnerabilis（易受伤的）← 拉丁语 vulnerō（使受伤）← vulnus（伤口）
column3: easily harmed or attacked
column5: Young plants are vulnerable to frost.|The system is vulnerable to attack.
column6: open to being wounded, with little to protect it – 敞着口，没什么护着，容易挨伤
column7: 易受伤的：容易受到损害|脆弱的：本身经不住外力

column2: 中古英语 wage ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 wage ← 诺曼法语 wage（古法语 gauge 的北部变体）← 法兰克语 *wadi（抵押）← 原始日耳曼语 *wadją（担保）；与 wed 同支
column3: money paid regularly for work done
column5: Wages rose by three percent.|He earns a weekly wage.
column6: the sum pledged for work and paid at set times – 为劳务许下、按期付出的那笔钱
column7: 工资：按劳付给的报酬|薪水：同义，多用于固定发放的那种

column2: 借自中古荷兰语 wagen ← 原始日耳曼语 *wagnaz（车）← 原始印欧语 *weǵʰ-（运送）；取代了本土同源词 wain
column3: a vehicle with four wheels for carrying loads
column5: A horse pulled the wagon uphill.|Coal came in open wagons.
column6: a four-wheeled body built to carry loads – 四轮的车身，专为载重而造
column7: 大车：马拉的那种四轮载货车|货车厢：火车上装货的那节车厢

column2: 中古英语 wast ← 古英语 *wæst ← 原始西日耳曼语 *wahstu ← 原始日耳曼语 *wahstuz（长成、身量）← 原始印欧语 *h₂weks-（增长）；与 wax（渐长）同支
column3: the narrow part of the body between the ribs and the hips
column5: The dress is tight at the waist.|He measured his waist with a tape.
column6: the narrow part of the body between ribs and hips – 肋与髋之间收窄的那一段身体
column7: 腰：身体中段收细处|腰部：同一处，说得更正式

column2: 中古英语 waiten ← 盎格鲁诺曼语 waiter ← 法兰克语 *wahtwēn（守望）← 原始日耳曼语 *wahtwō（守卫）← 原始印欧语 *weǵ-（清醒、警觉）；与 watch 同支
column3: to stay where one is until something happens
column5: We waited an hour for the bus.|Wait here until I call you.
column6: staying put because what you need has not come – 该来的还没来，就守在原处不动
column7: 等：停在原处不走|等候：语气较正式，多指等人或消息|等待：把这段停留说得更书面

column2: 14 世纪末的中古英语 waiter（侍从、守望者），即 wait ＋ -er；「餐桌侍者」义 15 世纪末始见
column3: a man who serves food at tables in a restaurant
column5: The waiter brought the menu at once.|He worked as a waiter that summer.
column6: one who stands by the table to serve those eating – 守在桌边伺候进餐的人
column7: 男服务员：餐厅里上菜的那位男性|侍者：偏书面，不分性别时也用

column2: 由 waiter ＋ 阴性后缀 -ess 构成，1834 年始见记载
column3: a woman who serves food at tables in a restaurant
column5: A waitress took their order.|She trained the new waitresses herself.
column6: a woman who stands by the table to serve those eating – 守在桌边伺候进餐的女性

column2: 中古英语 waken ← 古英语 wacan／wacian（醒来、守夜）← 原始日耳曼语 *wakaną ← 原始印欧语 *weǵ-（清醒）
column3: to stop sleeping, or to make someone stop sleeping
column5: She woke before the alarm rang.|Try not to wake the baby.
column6: passing from sleep back into awareness – 从睡里回到有知觉的状态
column7: 醒：自己不再睡|唤醒：使别人不再睡|醒来：强调由睡转醒那一刻

column2: 中古英语 waknen ← 古英语 wæcnan ← 原始日耳曼语 *waknaną（醒）← 原始印欧语 *weǵ-（清醒）
column3: to wake, or to rouse someone from sleep
column5: The noise wakened the whole house.|He wakened slowly and sat up.
column6: bringing someone out of sleep – 把人从睡中带出来
column7: 唤醒：叫某人醒过来|使苏醒：把昏睡或不振的状态带回清醒

column2: 中古英语 walken ← 古英语 wealcan（转动、滚）与 wealcian（卷、缠）合流 ← 原始日耳曼语 *walkaną（滚、行走）← 原始印欧语 *walg-（转、动）
column3: to move along on foot at a normal pace
column5: They walked home along the canal.|She walks to work every day.
column6: moving forward on foot, one leg after the other – 靠两条腿一前一后往前挪
column7: 走：用脚行进|步行：不借车马，全靠两腿|散步：为舒展而慢走一趟

column2: 中古英语 wal ← 古英语 weall（墙、堤、垒）← 原始西日耳曼语 *wall ← 拉丁语 vallum（土垒、栅墙）← 原始印欧语 *welH-（转、卷）
column3: an upright structure that encloses or divides a space
column5: A brick wall runs along the garden.|Hang the picture on that wall.
column6: an upright barrier that shuts one space off from another – 立起来的一道挡，把一处与另一处隔开
column7: 墙：房屋或院落的那道竖直结构|围墙：绕着一片地圈起来的那种|壁：室内的那一面，多用于复合词

column2: 中古英语 walet（口袋、行囊），更早词源不明；或出自诺曼法语 *walet（卷、袋）← 原始日耳曼语 *wal-（卷）
column3: a small flat folding case for money and cards
column5: He left his wallet in the taxi.|She kept photographs in her wallet.
column6: a small flat case folded over to hold money and cards – 对折的小扁夹，装钱与卡片
column7: 钱包：装钱和卡的那件小夹|票夹：专放票证的那种

column2: 中古英语 wandren ← 古英语 wandrian（漫游、飘荡）← 原始西日耳曼语 *wandarōn，即 *wandōn（转）＋ 反复体后缀 -rōn
column3: to move about without a fixed route or purpose
column5: They wandered through the old town.|His attention wandered during the talk.
column6: moving about with no set route to follow – 没有定好的路线，随处移动
column7: 漫步：不赶路地随意走|闲逛：走着看着，无固定去处|走神：注意力像人一样游走开去

column2: 中古英语 wanten（缺、需要）← 古诺尔斯语 vanta（缺）← 原始日耳曼语 *wanatōną（缺乏）← *wanô（欠缺）← 原始印欧语 *h₁weh₂-（空）
column3: to feel that you would like to have something
column5: I want a cup of tea.|The house wants a coat of paint.
column6: feeling the gap where something is missing – 感到有个缺口，那里少了点什么
column7: 想要：心里希望得到|需要：客观上少了它不行|缺少：本义即此，指欠着没有
